topic: Sukuna's full story from the Heian Era to the end of the Shinjuku Showdown, argued around one blind spot: the strongest sorcerer in history never understood what Yuji was
title: Sukuna Explained: The King of Curses' Full Story
description:
Sukuna is Jujutsu Kaisen's King of Curses, the strongest sorcerer in history. This is his full story in order: the Heian Era legend, his deal with Kenjaku, the finger Yuji Itadori swallowed, Shibuya, the takeover of Megumi, the fight against Satoru Gojo, and the raid that finally caught up with him.

Every chapter number comes from the wiki, so jump to any part of Sukuna's power, techniques and history you came here for. The thread running through all of it is one blind spot, and by the end I think you will see why it mattered more than any technique he owned.
comment: Was Sukuna's real weakness his arrogance, or the fact he never understood anyone who fought for something other than himself? Pick one.

lines.text: Sukuna was the King of Curses, unbeaten for a thousand years, and what finally broke him wasn't power at all.

shot.fallback: towering four-armed sorcerer king looming over a ruined city

lines.text: Here is Sukuna's whole story, from the Heian Era to Shinjuku, with a chapter number behind every claim.

shot.fallback: dark spirit rising behind a teenage boy

lines.text: So how does history's strongest sorcerer lose to a teenager he never once took seriously?

shot.fallback: tyrant staring down a determined teenager

lines.text: My answer is one blind spot, and it was sitting inside his own vessel from chapter 1.

shot.fallback: smirking king in a shrine of blades

lines.text: It starts a thousand years ago, with a man most fans still picture as a demon...

shot.fallback: ancient Japanese capital under a red sky

lines.text: Forget the legend for a second, because the legend gets the most important fact about Sukuna wrong.

shot.fallback: old scroll painting of a four-armed demon

lines.text: Stories call him a demon born in the Heian Era, an imaginary monster with four arms and two faces.

shot.fallback: monstrous four-armed figure in ancient robes

lines.text: The wiki is blunt about it: he was a human sorcerer, undefeated, whom people called the Disgraced One in chapter 199.

shot.fallback: grim ancient sorcerer sitting on a throne

lines.text: That matters, because a human has a childhood, and a childhood leaves marks that a monster would never carry.

shot.fallback: lonely child standing in an empty ancient hall

lines.text: Hold on to that, because chapter 237 drops a hint that even Sukuna resented the way he was raised.

shot.fallback: brooding king looking at the ground

lines.text: In the Golden Age of Jujutsu, every sorcerer alive was sharpening their skills for the sole purpose of taking him down.

shot.fallback: ancient sorcerers charging a lone figure

lines.text: He beat thousands of them, and every loss only sharpened him, which is a frightening way to build a legend.

shot.fallback: lone warrior standing among defeated rivals

lines.text: Chapters 219 and 238 give the clearest scoreboard: he took on the Sun, Moon, and Stars Squad all by himself.

shot.search: Sukuna Sun Moon and Stars Squad
shot.fallback: elite ancient squad facing a four-armed king

lines.text: Then he did the same to the Five Empty Generals, the most elite fighters the Fujiwara Clan had to offer.

shot.fallback: five armored generals standing in formation

lines.text: Those defeats terrified Japan's authorities so badly that they were willing to hold festivals in his honor.

shot.fallback: festival lanterns and bowing nobles in ancient Japan

lines.text: Think about that: the government of the age was throwing celebrations for the one man nobody could stop.

shot.fallback: king receiving offerings from frightened officials

lines.text: And the body behind all of it was unmistakable: four arms, four eyes, and a second mouth across his stomach.

shot.fallback: four-armed man with a mouth on his torso

lines.text: He could use all four arms independently, with two making hand signs while the mouth on his stomach chanted nonstop.

shot.search: Sukuna four arms hand signs chant
shot.fallback: four-armed sorcerer weaving hand signs

lines.text: Even his archery was flawless, which we only learn when Yuji's own domain shows him hitting the bullseye.

shot.fallback: archer drawing a bow at a target

lines.text: He also took in a child named Uraume, first to chill his food, and eventually as a loyal subordinate.

shot.fallback: pale child bringing food to a towering king

lines.text: So the first thing to understand is that the King of Curses wasn't born a monster in somebody's story.

shot.fallback: stoic ancient king with tattoos

lines.text: He was a man who won every fight he ever took, and nothing in his life ever forced him to change.

shot.fallback: victorious warrior in a silent battlefield

lines.text: Even Satoru Gojo, the strongest sorcerer of the modern age, admits a fight against him would be difficult.

shot.fallback: white-haired sorcerer eyeing a looming rival

lines.text: Hundreds of years of sorcerers tried to catch up to him, and none of them could reach his level.

shot.fallback: king standing above a sea of challengers

lines.text: The wiki calls him egocentric, hedonistic, and exceptionally sadistic, and that personality never changes across a thousand years.

shot.fallback: grinning king lounging on a throne

lines.text: He likens human beings to insects, and he admits he cannot comprehend why the weak cling so desperately to life.

shot.fallback: king looking down at tiny distant figures

lines.text: He also claims to have no dreams, goals, or aspirations, while the sorcerers fighting him have them and grow stronger because of it.

shot.fallback: king shrugging while heroes train in the distance

lines.text: Yet the wiki is careful to say none of this is stupidity, because he is highly intelligent and manipulative underneath the swagger.

shot.fallback: king smiling with calculating eyes

lines.text: He barely follows the modern world, and in chapter 112 he glances at a smartphone and calls it a phone with a camera.

shot.fallback: king squinting at a glowing phone screen

lines.text: But a man like that doesn't just fade away when his body gives out, and Sukuna had a plan for that...

shot.fallback: two ancient sorcerers sharing a quiet bargain

lines.text: The plan had a name attached to it, and that name is Kenjaku, a sorcerer who had already been alive for ages.

shot.fallback: stitched-scalp sorcerer smiling in candlelight

lines.text: In chapter 158, we learn that Sukuna accepted a proposal from Kenjaku to take part in the Culling Game.

shot.fallback: ancient king listening to a smiling schemer

lines.text: That sounds like a strange thing for the strongest sorcerer alive to agree to, so ask what Kenjaku actually offered him.

shot.fallback: smiling schemer offering a king a secret deal

lines.text: The offer was survival, because Kenjaku knew how to turn a sorcerer into a cursed object after they were gone.

shot.fallback: glowing mummified finger in a dark box

lines.text: Chapter 228 says it flatly: Kenjaku is the only person who knows how, and Sukuna didn't know it in the Heian Era.

shot.fallback: schemer teaching a king a forbidden technique

lines.text: So the King of Curses, who learned everything just by seeing it, had to rely on someone else for the one trick that mattered.

shot.fallback: tyrant reluctantly leaning on a clever ally

lines.text: The result is the thing the whole series is built on: his soul and cursed energy split across twenty indestructible fingers.

shot.fallback: twenty glowing mummified fingers scattered across a map

lines.text: According to the Angel inside Hana Kurusu in chapter 220, Sukuna later picked up the idea of splitting his soul after experiencing it once.

shot.fallback: glowing angelic figure explaining a secret to a girl

lines.text: That detail will matter later, so file it away, because it is how he ends up jumping bodies at the worst possible moment.

shot.fallback: glowing finger being passed between two silhouettes

lines.text: Notice something about the deal itself: Sukuna isn't scheming for power, because he already had more than anyone.

shot.fallback: king resting his chin on his fist

lines.text: Each of the twenty fingers holds a piece of his cursed energy and soul, which is why one swallowed finger changes everything.

shot.fallback: glowing finger radiating dark energy

lines.text: The fingers are described as indestructible, so nobody could simply destroy the problem, and they had to be collected instead.

shot.fallback: stone box holding a glowing finger that will not break

lines.text: And the arrangement wasn't only with Kenjaku, since Uraume was also left waiting, loyal to their master across the centuries.

shot.fallback: pale figure waiting patiently beside a sealed box

lines.text: He agreed to hold on to existence itself, and I think that says he simply enjoyed fighting too much to stop.

shot.fallback: grinning tyrant cracking his knuckles

lines.text: That fits the personality the wiki describes, a glutton for fighting who draws out fights with strong opponents on purpose.

shot.fallback: king savoring a fight with a cruel smile

lines.text: Kenjaku needed that bargain to hold, and chapter 221 shows how far Sukuna will go to keep it.

shot.fallback: schemer standing behind a towering protector

lines.text: In chapter 221, Sukuna protects Kenjaku from Gojo, and agrees not to fight Kenjaku until their agreement is finished.

shot.fallback: king blocking an attacker to protect an ally

lines.text: That is the only time we see a Sukuna that honors a bargain, and it tells you how seriously he took this one.

shot.fallback: two figures shaking hands in shadow

lines.text: More than a thousand years pass, the fingers get scattered, and the King of Curses waits as a collection of cursed objects.

shot.fallback: sealed finger resting in a stone box

lines.text: Nothing about this waiting looks like a man at peace, though, because a cursed object is still awake in its own way.

shot.fallback: faintly glowing relic in a dark room

lines.text: So here's the question nobody asks: what kind of person swallows a finger like that on purpose?

shot.fallback: teenager holding up a withered finger

lines.text: Because in June 2018, that is exactly what a teenager in Sendai does...

lines.text: In chapter 227, Gojo changes the conditions of his domain, and even Kusakabe, an expert on barriers, is astonished.

shot.fallback: veteran swordsman astonished by a glowing barrier

lines.text: Then in chapter 232, Gojo lands a Black Flash when Sukuna least expects it, and it knocks him unconscious.

shot.fallback: black lightning striking a king's face

lines.text: Gojo also did what Yuji and Maki could not, which is injure Sukuna critically using martial arts alone.

shot.fallback: white-haired sorcerer striking a king in close combat

lines.text: Sukuna's own Dismantle and Cleave can cut skyscrapers in half, and Yuta's Cleave only left minor cuts on Sukuna's face in chapter 250.

shot.fallback: thin blades splitting a tower in half

lines.text: Kashimo watches Sukuna shift between Domain Amplification and his technique without a flaw, and he is astonished.

shot.fallback: lightning sorcerer watching a king shift techniques

lines.text: Sukuna can even keep his own heart beating with cursed energy after it is pierced, which the wiki notes in chapter 252.

shot.fallback: king smirking with a glowing chest

lines.text: So at this point of the fight, Gojo is winning, and I think anyone watching would have bet on it.

shot.fallback: sorcerer standing over a stunned king

lines.text: By the end, Sukuna will have expanded his domain three times in this one fight.

shot.fallback: king raising a domain again with a grin

lines.text: Even so, the wiki says his cursed energy only dropped to Yuta's level, which was enough for two more domains.

shot.fallback: king with a steady aura after a long fight

lines.text: That's the thing about this duel: Gojo has to be perfect for every second, and Sukuna only has to be right once.

shot.fallback: two fighters circling each other in rubble

lines.text: Gojo never shows signs of tiring either, and the wiki says he reinforced himself and activated techniques over and over without running dry.

shot.fallback: sorcerer glowing steadily during a long fight

lines.text: Gojo then fires an unlimited Hollow Purple in chapter 234, and it wipes out Mahoraga and a large part of Shinjuku.

shot.fallback: enormous purple blast flattening a city district

lines.text: The wiki says that Hollow Purple destroyed Mahoraga completely and decimated a large area of Shinjuku.

shot.fallback: crater where a city district used to be

lines.text: Sukuna survives it barely, standing with severe injuries and one chance left to turn the match around.

shot.fallback: battered king struggling to stand in rubble

lines.text: This is the moment the fight is decided, and what Sukuna does next is make a binding vow.

lines.text: He makes a vow that lets him bypass the conditions of the world-cutting technique and fire it, per chapter 255's recap.

shot.fallback: king clenching his fist as glowing chains form

lines.text: In chapter 236, it lands when Gojo least expects it, and the strongest sorcerer of the modern age is cut in two.

shot.fallback: white-haired sorcerer staring in disbelief as a cutting approaches

lines.text: Keep that image in mind, because Sukuna won the fight he was supposed to lose on paper.

shot.fallback: king standing alone in a ruined city

lines.text: Stack up everything in this fight and you'll notice Gojo never lost on power, he lost on one moment.

shot.fallback: sorcerer realizing too late

lines.text: That is a very Sukuna way to win: patient, opportunistic, and smart enough to turn a single mistake into a victory.

shot.fallback: grinning king with his arms crossed

lines.text: But the King of Curses has just erased the one person who respected him as an equal, and he doesn't know it yet...

shot.fallback: king staring at the empty space where a rival stood

lines.text: With Gojo gone, the raid on Sukuna moves into its next phase, and the next sorcerers in line are far weaker.

shot.fallback: group of sorcerers assembling for a final stand

lines.text: That's exactly where Hajime Kashimo steps in, a sorcerer from 400 years ago who entered the Culling Game just to fight Sukuna.

shot.fallback: lightning-clad sorcerer facing a tired king

lines.text: In chapter 237, Kashimo pressures Sukuna so hard that he is forced to finish his incarnation.

shot.fallback: lightning beast pushing a king backward

lines.text: He asks Sukuna a question that fits our theme: was Sukuna born the strongest, or did he earn it?

shot.fallback: lightning sorcerer asking a king a quiet question

lines.text: Kashimo also asks if true strength means solitude, if it's a cross the strongest must carry.

shot.fallback: lonely warrior kneeling before a king

lines.text: In chapter 238, Sukuna answers that connecting with others by showing your strength is a kind of love.

shot.fallback: king speaking gently to a defeated challenger

lines.text: The wiki adds that Sukuna sees responding in kind to sorcerers who sharpened themselves to kill him as his way of connection.

shot.fallback: king surrounded by challengers with a calm face

lines.text: That might be the most honest thing he says in the whole story, and also the most revealing.

shot.fallback: king with a rare quiet expression

lines.text: The wiki adds that he considers love worthless and hates the idea of needing another person to satisfy him.

shot.fallback: king scoffing at an outstretched hand

lines.text: His idea of a relationship is a fight, and his idea of respect is making someone's best effort matter.

shot.fallback: king nodding to a kneeling rival

lines.text: Which means he has no way to read someone who doesn't fight him to win a relationship at all.

shot.fallback: king puzzled at a boy who refuses to fight like others

lines.text: And that matters, because Yuji's cursed energy came from pieces of Sukuna himself, and he kept a huge pool even after Sukuna left.

shot.fallback: boy glowing with dark energy

lines.text: That's Yuji, and he's about to become Sukuna's biggest problem, one chapter at a time.

shot.fallback: determined boy racing toward a tall king

lines.text: With his full body unlocked, Sukuna can outrun Yuji, and he's using hand-to-hand and Black Flash on the raid.

shot.fallback: black lightning punch sending a woman flying

lines.text: His first Black Flash lands on Maki Zenin in chapter 253, and he'll land seven in the whole battle.

shot.fallback: black sparks surrounding a king's fist

lines.text: He hits Larue next, then Maki again, then Choso, then Yuji, then Todo, and then Hana.

lines.text: That string of hits disrupts Sukuna's connection with Megumi's soul and lowers his cursed energy output and control.

lines.text: Larue's Cutie Honey distracts the King in chapter 256, and that gives Yuji the opening for his very first Black Flash against him.

shot.fallback: cheerful sorcerer waving a distraction at a king

lines.text: I think this is where the story proves its theory: the weaker man on paper, the one he dismisses, keeps landing blows.

shot.fallback: teenager landing a clean hit on a stunned king

lines.text: Even so, Sukuna fights back with improvised binding vows that remove everyone from the battlefield except Yuji.

shot.fallback: king raising a domain as allies disappear

lines.text: Those vows let him expand his domain without lowering its output, and he tilts the fight right back.

shot.fallback: king smiling inside a freshly opened shrine

lines.text: Later, in chapter 260, Todo's Boogie Woogie provides the distraction for Yuji's eighth Black Flash, landing right on Sukuna's chest.

lines.text: Chapter 258 shows what Sukuna does when cornered: he's flexible, clever, and ruthless about the rules.

shot.fallback: king rewriting the rules mid-fight

lines.text: Meanwhile, Yuta decides he needs Sukuna's technique, and in chapter 267 Yuji gives up his left ring finger.

lines.text: Megumi, trapped inside, regains his will after Yuji reaches him, and holds Sukuna in place with his own technique.

shot.fallback: shadow hands gripping a king from within

lines.text: That moment turns the raid, because it proves Sukuna's greatest hold on Megumi was despair, and despair can be reversed.

shot.fallback: student rising with new resolve inside a dark void

lines.text: And the final fight, the one that ended the King, happens in a place that belongs to Yuji alone...

shot.fallback: teenager opening a glowing domain over a field

lines.text: Yuji's Domain Expansion is chapter 265, and he doesn't use it to hurt Sukuna, he uses it to show him a place.

lines.text: Sukuna wanders through Yuji's childhood memories, with grasshoppers in the rice fields and the town he grew up in.

lines.text: The wiki says Yuji felt pity for him, and offered him one last chance to surrender out of mercy.

shot.fallback: teenager reaching out a hand to an angry king

lines.text: That's the thing the King of Curses can't handle: he's enraged by pity, because his identity is built on being strongest.

shot.fallback: furious king glaring at a kind teenager

lines.text: Offering mercy to Sukuna tells him he's weak, and in his own mind, nothing could be worse than that.

shot.fallback: king gritting his teeth in rage

lines.text: Chapter 248 gives the clearest hint: Yuji challenges Sukuna's worldview just by being his opposite.

shot.fallback: two silhouettes standing back to back in light and shadow

lines.text: The wiki says that fills Sukuna with a hatred he can't describe, unlike anything he has felt before.

shot.fallback: king trembling with unexplained fury

lines.text: Add the fact that Yuji is the grandson of Sukuna's reincarnated twin brother, as chapter 257 and volume 29 note.

shot.fallback: two faces side by side connected by a faint line

lines.text: Chapter 248 stresses the point: Yuji wins no argument with Sukuna, he just keeps being the opposite of him, again and again.

shot.fallback: boy standing firm against a looming king

lines.text: Even knowing that, Sukuna refuses to treat Yuji as a threat, which is the blind spot I've been pointing at all along.

shot.fallback: king waving off a teenager with a smirk

lines.text: He also admits in chapter 237 that his own upbringing left resentment, which is the closest he gets to describing what shaped him.

shot.fallback: king staring at an old memory

lines.text: He understood power, he understood technique, and he understood strategy, but he never understood what Yuji was fighting for.

shot.fallback: king staring at a boy he cannot read

lines.text: So when the final blows come, they come from the people he never counted: Nobara, Todo, and Yuta.

lines.text: Yuji separates Sukuna from Megumi's soul, and Sukuna can only tell him his attempts at leveling with him were a farce.

lines.text: Even in defeat, he refuses mercy, and he calls it a long-standing farce rather than admit Yuji got through.

lines.text: The wiki calls this his refusal of mercy on the verge of defeat, because accepting it would mean admitting Yuji won.

shot.fallback: king turning his face away

lines.text: Yuji, for his part, says the way someone dies doesn't matter, and that treating lives as worthless is the thing he can't stand.

shot.fallback: boy speaking quietly in a sunlit field

lines.text: He also now believes that living a mundane life still leaves value behind in the memories that continue after someone is gone.

shot.fallback: boy looking at drifting fragments of memory

lines.text: Megumi's will returns at the same time, and he says he'll go back to living for others before Sukuna is stripped away.

lines.text: After the separation, Megumi carries three scars matching the eyes of Sukuna's incarnated form, per chapter 268.

lines.text: Notice what that means: the King of Curses, even beaten, left a permanent mark on the one body he coveted.

lines.text: It's a small detail, but it says the incarnation was never a clean takeover, and neither was the loss.

shot.fallback: tired student looking at the sky

lines.text: Megumi is free of him afterward, but the three scars he carries are a permanent reminder of the King who lived inside him.

shot.fallback: student looking at his reflection quietly

lines.text: The last piece of the Culling Game falls with him too, since the Great Merger was prevented, according to chapter 270.

lines.text: Tengen's remains were left in Sukuna, so with his defeat the ritual lost its purpose.

lines.text: Kenjaku's failsafe moved Tengen's remains into Sukuna and gave him the authority to end the Culling Game, per chapter 248.

lines.text: So Kenjaku's whole ritual dies with Sukuna's defeat, but the King of Curses still has one last place to go...

shot.fallback: schemer watching his plan fall apart

lines.text: Sukuna's story doesn't end on the battlefield, because chapter 271 follows him into the passageway for souls.

lines.text: There, Mahito accuses him of lying to himself about wanting revenge on those who scorned him long ago.

lines.text: Sukuna doesn't deny it, which is the first time we see him choose honesty over pride.

lines.text: He even says that if he hadn't feared the flames of his own curse, he might have taken a less destructive path.

shot.fallback: king reflecting with tired eyes

lines.text: The wiki adds that he seems open to changing his ways if he is reincarnated, and he accepts his loss.

shot.fallback: king stepping calmly toward a bright light

lines.text: That is the closest this story gets to a redemption.

shot.fallback: patchwork curse lingering in a pale hall

lines.text: That contrast says a lot, because the curses who worshipped Sukuna never grasped the thing that finally moved him.

shot.fallback: two silhouettes parting ways in a pale hall

lines.text: Uraume, the child he once took in, is the one other soul who followed him from his own era.

shot.fallback: pale figure waiting beside a king

lines.text: Look back at Kashimo asking whether strength means being alone, because the ending suggests Sukuna decided other people couldn't matter.

lines.text: So here is my verdict on how the strongest sorcerer in history was beaten: he was never beaten by strength.

lines.text: The first piece of evidence is chapter 8, where he treated Yuji's life as a bargaining chip.

lines.text: The second is Shibuya, where he used Yuji's body and then handed it back, expecting guilt to finish the job.

shot.fallback: king smirking at a broken boy

lines.text: The third is the Gojo fight, where he won, and then trusted that every other sorcerer was just more of the same.

shot.fallback: king surveying new challengers with contempt

lines.text: The fourth is the final fight, where pity from the one person he refused to respect was the thing he could not survive.

lines.text: Now the strongest counter-argument: some fans say Sukuna lost because he was weakened by the vessel swap and Gojo's damage.

lines.text: Power was never the problem, so the blind spot argument still holds, and I think it's the better explanation.
